updateTarget.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function

tasks.goal: Create the trial function from scratch in eu-west-2 with the current Node.js 24 runtime and the default minimal execution role.
tasks.title: TEST

cleanup.title: Delete the Lambda function
cleanup.description: In Lambda in eu-west-2, open follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions > Delete, enter the requested name, and confirm.
cleanup.instruction: In Lambda in eu-west-2, open follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions > Delete, enter the requested name, and confirm.
cleanup.verification: Search the eu-west-2 Functions list for follow-along-lambda-area and confirm that no result appears.

consoleSteps.title: Open Lambda in the correct Region
consoleSteps.warning: Do not continue in a different Region, because later searches and cleanup would not find the same resources.
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to the AWS Management Console. Use the Region selector to choose Europe (London) eu-west-2. In the search bar enter Lambda, then open the Lambda service.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console. Use the Region selector to choose Europe (London) eu-west-2. In the search bar enter Lambda, then open the Lambda service.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Lambda Functions page opens and the Region selector shows Europe (London).

consoleSteps.title: Create the function from scratch
consoleSteps.warning: Use exactly this trial name so the log group and cleanup checks are easy to identify.
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Create function. Select Author from scratch. Set Function name to follow-along-lambda-area. Select Runtime Node.js 24.x and Architecture x86_64. Keep the default option to create a new role with basic Lambda permissions, then choose Create function.

instructions.text: Choose Create function. Select Author from scratch. Set Function name to follow-along-lambda-area. Select Runtime Node.js 24.x and Architecture x86_64. Keep the default option to create a new role with basic Lambda permissions, then choose Create function.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function page opens for follow-along-lambda-area and shows a successful creation message.

consoleSteps.title: Replace the starter code
consoleSteps.instruction: In the Code tab, open index.mjs. Replace the editor contents with: export const handler = async (event) => { const area = event.length * event.width; console.log(`The area is ${area}`); return area; };

instructions.text: In the Code tab, open index.mjs. Replace the editor contents with: export const handler = async (event) => { const area = event.length * event.width; console.log(`The area is ${area}`); return area; };

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The editor shows an exported handler that multiplies event.length by event.width, records the area and returns it.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy the code
consoleSteps.warning: Editing the code is not enough; the Deploy action must succeed before testing.
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Deploy above the code editor and wait for the update to finish.

instructions.text: Choose Deploy above the code editor and wait for the update to finish.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A green message confirms that the function was updated successfully and the code is ready to test.

verification.title: Confirm the function and runtime
verification.instruction: On the function page, check the function name, Runtime settings and the latest deployment message.
verification.expectedResult: The page shows follow-along-lambda-area, Node.js 24.x, handler index.handler, and a successful deployment.

tasks.whyItMatters: This introduces the function, runtime, handler and execution-role boundary before any invocation occurs.

cli.reason: This beginner Follow Along uses the AWS Management Console so every action is visible; a CLI alternative is deliberately outside this trial.

tasks.goal: Create a private JSON test event with length 6 and width 7, invoke the function and confirm that it returns an area of 42.
tasks.title: Invoke the Function with a Test Event

cleanup.title: Remove the private test event with the function
cleanup.description: The area-test event is private configuration stored with follow-along-lambda-area. Deleting that function in the preceding cleanup action removes this event with it.
cleanup.instruction: The area-test event is private configuration stored with follow-along-lambda-area. Deleting that function in the preceding cleanup action removes this event with it.
cleanup.verification: The function search returns no result, so its private area-test event can no longer be selected or invoked.

tasks.feature: Lambda test events and synchronous invocation

consoleSteps.title: Create a private test event
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put passwords, keys or personal information in a test event.
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Test tab, choose Create new event, select Private, enter Event name area-test, and use this JSON: { "length": 6, "width": 7 }. Choose Save.

instructions.text: Open the Test tab, choose Create new event, select Private, enter Event name area-test, and use this JSON: { "length": 6, "width": 7 }. Choose Save.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The saved event named area-test is selected and the editor shows length 6 and width 7.

consoleSteps.title: Invoke the function
consoleSteps.warning: If the result is not 42, return to the Code tab, compare the handler carefully, choose Deploy, and test again.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Execution result reports Succeeded and the function response is 42.

verification.title: Confirm the area result
verification.instruction: Select area-test on the Test tab and choose Test. Expand Execution result if needed.
verification.expectedResult: Status is Succeeded, the response is 42, and the event contains length 6 and width 7.

tasks.whyItMatters: A controlled test event proves how Lambda passes JSON input to the handler and shows the invocation result before monitoring.

cli.reason: The console test-event workflow is the clearest beginner path; CLI invocation is deliberately outside this trial.

tasks.goal: Open the function Monitor tab, follow View CloudWatch logs and find the log stream containing the successful invocation and calculated area.
tasks.title: Inspect the Invocation in CloudWatch Logs

cleanup.title: Delete the Lambda log group
cleanup.description: In CloudWatch in eu-west-2, choose Logs > Log groups, select /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions > Delete log group, and confirm.
cleanup.instruction: In CloudWatch in eu-west-2, choose Logs > Log groups, select /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions > Delete log group, and confirm.
cleanup.verification: Search Log groups for /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area and confirm that no result appears.

consoleSteps.title: Open the function logs
consoleSteps.warning: CloudWatch logs can take 5 to 10 minutes to appear after the first invocation.
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Monitor tab on follow-along-lambda-area, then choose View CloudWatch logs.

instructions.text: Open the Monitor tab on follow-along-lambda-area, then choose View CloudWatch logs.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudWatch opens the /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area log group in Europe (London).

consoleSteps.title: Open the newest log stream
consoleSteps.instruction: In Log streams, choose the stream with the most recent Last event time.

instructions.text: In Log streams, choose the stream with the most recent Last event time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The stream displays log events for the test invocation.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm the invocation evidence
consoleSteps.warning: If the stream is empty, wait briefly, refresh the list and open the newest stream again.
consoleSteps.instruction: Find the message The area is 42 and the START, END and REPORT records for the same invocation.

instructions.text: Find the message The area is 42 and the START, END and REPORT records for the same invocation.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The custom log message and Lambda request and duration records confirm that the tested invocation ran successfully.

verification.title: Confirm the invocation log
verification.instruction: Open the newest stream in /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area and inspect the most recent event records.
verification.expectedResult: The stream contains The area is 42 plus START, END and REPORT records for a successful request.

tasks.whyItMatters: Logs provide the evidence needed to troubleshoot a serverless function and connect an invocation result to its request and duration records.

cli.reason: The console links the function directly to its log group; CloudWatch Logs CLI queries are deliberately outside this beginner trial.

tasks.goal: Delete the trial Lambda function, its /aws/lambda/<function-name> log group and its generated execution role, then verify that all three are gone.
tasks.title: Delete the Trial Lambda Resources

cleanup.title: Check regional cleanup before removing IAM permissions
cleanup.description: Confirm that follow-along-lambda-area is absent from Lambda Functions and /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area is absent from CloudWatch Log groups in eu-west-2.
cleanup.instruction: Confirm that follow-along-lambda-area is absent from Lambda Functions and /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area is absent from CloudWatch Log groups in eu-west-2.
cleanup.verification: The function and log-group searches return no matching trial resource, so the generated role can now be removed.

tasks.feature: Lambda, CloudWatch Logs and IAM cleanup

consoleSteps.title: Record the generated role name
consoleSteps.warning: Record only the role name; do not copy credentials or secret values.
consoleSteps.instruction: Before deleting the function, open Configuration, choose Permissions, and copy the Execution role name into a temporary note.

instructions.text: Before deleting the function, open Configuration, choose Permissions, and copy the Execution role name into a temporary note.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You have the exact generated role name needed for the final IAM cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the Lambda function
consoleSteps.warning: Deleting the function does not automatically remove its CloudWatch log group or generated IAM role.
consoleSteps.instruction: Return to the function page, choose Actions, choose Delete, enter follow-along-lambda-area when asked, and confirm Delete.

instructions.text: Return to the function page, choose Actions, choose Delete, enter follow-along-lambda-area when asked, and confirm Delete.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Functions list no longer contains follow-along-lambda-area.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the CloudWatch log group
consoleSteps.instruction: Open CloudWatch, choose Logs, choose Log groups, select /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions, Delete log group, and confirm.

instructions.text: Open CloudWatch, choose Logs, choose Log groups, select /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, choose Actions, Delete log group, and confirm.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Searching Log groups for follow-along-lambda-area returns no result.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the generated execution role
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the role created for this trial. Do not delete any shared or unfamiliar role.
consoleSteps.instruction: Open IAM, choose Roles, search for the role name you recorded, open it, choose Delete, enter the requested confirmation text, and confirm.

instructions.text: Open IAM, choose Roles, search for the role name you recorded, open it, choose Delete, enter the requested confirmation text, and confirm.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Searching IAM Roles for the recorded role name returns no result.

consoleSteps.title: Verify the account is clean
consoleSteps.instruction: Return to Lambda in Europe (London) and search Functions for follow-along-lambda-area. Then repeat the CloudWatch log-group search and IAM role search.

instructions.text: Return to Lambda in Europe (London) and search Functions for follow-along-lambda-area. Then repeat the CloudWatch log-group search and IAM role search.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: All three searches return no trial resource, completing the cleanup.

verification.title: Confirm every trial resource is gone
verification.instruction: Search Lambda Functions in eu-west-2 for follow-along-lambda-area, CloudWatch Log groups for /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, and IAM Roles for the saved generated role name.
verification.expectedResult: Each search returns no matching trial resource.

tasks.whyItMatters: Cleanup prevents avoidable charges, removes account clutter and retires permissions that the finished practice project no longer needs.

cli.reason: Cleanup is shown in the console to reduce the chance of deleting the wrong resource; CLI deletion is deliberately outside this beginner trial.

phases.title: Test
phases.description: Create a beginner Lambda function from scratch with the current Node.js runtime and a minimal default execution role.

phases.title: TEST
phases.description: Invoke the function with a saved JSON event, confirm the returned area and inspect the matching CloudWatch invocation logs.

phases.title: asdasdadasdasdadsdad
phases.description: Remove the Lambda function, its generated CloudWatch log group and its generated execution role, then verify the resources are gone.

steps.title: Delete the generated execution role
steps.description: In IAM Roles, search for the exact execution role name saved from the function Permissions page. Open only that role, choose Delete, complete the confirmation, and delete it.
steps.instruction: In IAM Roles, search for the exact execution role name saved from the function Permissions page. Open only that role, choose Delete, complete the confirmation, and delete it.
steps.verification: Search IAM Roles again for the saved role name and confirm that no result appears.

steps.title: Verify the whole trial is removed
steps.description: Search Lambda Functions in eu-west-2 for follow-along-lambda-area, CloudWatch Log groups for /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, and IAM Roles for the saved generated role name.
steps.instruction: Search Lambda Functions in eu-west-2 for follow-along-lambda-area, CloudWatch Log groups for /aws/lambda/follow-along-lambda-area, and IAM Roles for the saved generated role name.
steps.verification: All searches return no result; the private area-test event is also gone with the deleted function.

warnings.cost: AWS Lambda includes a free tier, but related services and future usage can create charges. Complete every cleanup step as soon as the practice is finished.
warnings.region: Create, inspect and delete regional resources in Europe (London), eu-west-2. IAM is global, so verify the saved role name carefully.
warnings.safety: Cleanup is manual only. Check the exact resource name and Region before each deletion, and never remove a shared or unfamiliar resource.
warnings.credentials: Never paste access keys, secret keys, passwords, tokens or private data into the function code, test event, notes or this Follow Along.
